lead_time_analysis.stability: moderate — occasional spikes to ~4.7 WD observed

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.33 days

narrative: Material PL1__MAF7F411 exhibits continuous daily demand averaging 1,569 units/day with moderate variability (CV=0.23) across 216 working days. Lead times average 1.33 working days with occasional spikes. The current SAP policy of ordering at MOQ=132 generates ~3,090 orders/year, driving excessive ordering costs. The recommended (r,Q) policy consolidates replenishments into ~71 orders/year at 5,752 units each, buffered by a 2,335-unit safety stock calibrated to the 95% service level, while respecting the 8,087-unit storage ceiling.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binds: order quantity reduced from unconstrained EOQ 6,872 to 5,752 units to satisfy safety_stock + order_quantity <= 8,086.99

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous and near-normally distributed with moderate CV (0.23), lead times are short and observable — ideal conditions for the classical (r,Q) reorder-point model. The EOQ minimises combined ordering and holding costs; the reorder point provides the service-level guarantee.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 8,087 units reduces the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ (6,872 units). This slightly increases ordering frequency (~71 vs. ~59 orders/year) and marginally raises annual ordering cost, but the policy remains near-optimal and fully feasible.
